title: Do negative reward-prediction errors drive the learned rise in social actions?
question: An exploratory probe (FINDINGS_K, seeds 900-902) found that ~58% of learning updates carry a negative RPE and that locomotion, which fires ~8x more than social populations, absorbs most of the resulting depression. If negative RPEs are ignored (only positive RPEs change weights), does the learning-induced rise in attacking, signalling and sharing disappear, and do locomotion weights now grow more than social ones?
background: Experiments I-K: the rise in social behaviour under learning comes from a fall in total locomotion drive. Intervention: positive_rpe_only=true skips every weight update whose RPE is negative. Prediction from the candidate mechanism: activity-weighted potentiation now favours the most active pathways (locomotion), so social actions win less often than without learning or no more often. Seeds 1000-1007 have never been run.

hypotheses.statement: Ignoring negative RPEs lowers the attack rate
Ignoring negative RPEs lowers sharing given a neighbour in reach
With positive RPEs only, locomotion inputs grow more than social inputs
With positive RPEs only, learning does not raise the attack rate above no-learning
